title: cfgutils Module
content_markdown: Useful extensions for the server configuration.
overview: Useful extensions for the server configuration.
how_it_works:
The cfgutils module can be used to introduce randomness to the behaviour of the server. It provides setup functions and the “rand\_event” function. This function return either true or false, depending on a random value and a specified probability. E.g. if you set via fifo or script a probability value of 5%, then 5% of all calls to rand\_event will return false. The pseudovariable “$RANDOM” could be used to introduce random values e.g. into a SIP reply.

The benefit of this module is the probability of the decision can be manipulated by external applications such as web interface or command line tools. The probability must be specified as percent value, ranging from 0 to 100.

The module exports commands to FIFO server that can be used to change the global settings via FIFO interface. The FIFO commands are: “set\_prob”, “reset\_prob” and “get\_prob”.

This module can be used for simple load-shedding, e.g. reply 5% of the Invites with a 503 error and a adequate random Retry-After value.

The module provides as well functions to delay the execution of the server. The functions “sleep” and “usleep” could be used to let the server wait a specific time interval.

It can also hash the config file used from the server with a (weak) cryptographic hash function on startup. This value is saved and can be later compared to the actual hash, to detect modifications of this file after the server start. This functions are available as the FIFO commands “check\_config\_hash” and “get\_config\_hash”.

exported_parameters.name: initial_probability
exported_parameters.description: The initial value of the probability.

exported_parameters.name: hash_file
exported_parameters.description: The config file name for that a hash value should be calculated on startup.

exported_parameters.name: shv_hash_size
exported_parameters.description: The size of the hash table used to store the shared variables ($shv).

exported_parameters.name: shvset
exported_parameters.description:
Set the value of a shared variable ($shv(name)). The parameter can be set many times.

The value of the parameter has the format: _name_ '=' _type_ ':' _value_

*   _name_: shared variable name
    
*   _type_: type of the value
    
    *   “i”: integer value
        
    *   “s”: string value
        
    
*   _value_: value to be set

exported_parameters.name: varset
exported_parameters.description:
Set the value of a script variable ($var(name)). The parameter can be set many times.

The value of the parameter has the format: _name_ '=' _type_ ':' _value_

*   _name_: shared variable name
    
*   _type_: type of the value
    
    *   “i”: integer value
        
    *   “s”: string value
        
    
*   _value_: value to be set

exported_parameters.name: lock_pool_size
exported_parameters.description: The number of dynamic script locks to be allocated at OpenSIPS startup. This number must be a power of 2. (i.e. 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 ...)
exported_parameters.notes: Note that the _lock\_pool\_size_ parameter only affects the number of dynamic locks created at startup. The pool of static locks only depends on the number of unique static strings supplied throughout the script to the set of static lock functions.

exported_functions.name: rand_event

return_values.condition: if the generated random value is less or equal to the currently set probability

exported_functions.description: Generates a random floating point value between 0 - 100 and returns true if the value is less or equal to the currently set probability. If "probability" parameter is given, it will override the global parameter set by rand_set_prob().

exported_functions.name: rand_reset_prob
exported_functions.description: Reset the probability back to the initial_probability value.

exported_functions.name: rand_get_prob
exported_functions.description: Return the current probability setting, e.g. for logging purposes.

exported_functions.name: abort
exported_functions.description: Debugging function that aborts the server. Depending on the configuration of the server a core dump will be created.

exported_functions.name: pkg_status
exported_functions.description: Debugging function that dumps the status for the private (PKG) memory. This information is logged to the default log facility, depending on the general log level and the memlog setting. You need to compile the server with activated memory debugging to get detailed informations.

exported_functions.name: shm_status
exported_functions.description: Debugging function that dumps the status for the shared (SHM) memory. This information is logged to the default log facility, depending on the general log level and the memlog setting. You need to compile the server with activated memory debugging to get detailed informations.

exported_functions.name: set_count

parameters.name: var_to_count
parameters.description: The variable to count (e.g., AVPs, headers)

parameters.name: ret_var
parameters.description: The variable to store the result in

exported_functions.description: Counts the number of values of a given variable. It makes sense to call this function only for variables that can take more values (AVPs, headers). The result is returned in the second parameter.

exported_functions.name: set_select_weight

parameters.name: int_list_var
parameters.description: integer values of the given variable

exported_functions.description: This function selects an element from a set formed by the integer values of the given "int_list_var" variable. It applies the genetic algorithm - roulette-wheel selection to choose an element from a set. The probability of selecting a certain element is proportionate with its weight. It will return the index of that selected element.

exported_functions.name: ts_usec_delta

return_values.condition: difference overflows the signed integer holder (diff of ~35 minutes or more) when using delta_int

exported_functions.description: This function returns the absolute difference between the two given timestamps. The result is expressed as _microseconds_ and can be returned as either string or integer.

exported_functions.name: check_time_rec

parameters.name: time_string
parameters.description: Time recurrence string which will be matched against the current time. Its fields are separated by "|" and the order in which they are given is: "timezone | dtstart | dtend | duration | freq | until | interval | byday | bymday | byyday | byweekno | bymonth". None of the fields following "freq" is used unless "freq" is defined. If the string ends in multiple null fields, they can all be ommited. The "timezone" field is optional. It represents the timezone in which to interpret the time recurrence elements (e.g. dtstart, dtend, until). By default, the system time zone is used.

parameters.name: timestamp
parameters.description: A specific Unix time to check. The function simply expects the actual Unix time here, there is no need to perform any timezone adjustments.

exported_functions.description: The function returns a positive value if the specified time recurrence string matches the current time, or a negative value otherwise. For checking some other Unix timestamp than the current one, the second parameter will contain the intended timestamp to check. The syntax of each field is identical to the corresponding field from RFC 2445.

exported_functions.name: get_static_lock

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: key to be hashed in order to obtain the index of a static lock

exported_functions.description: Acquire the static lock which corresponds to "key". In case the lock is taken by another process, script execution will halt until the lock is released. Attempting to acquire the lock a second time by the same process, without releasing it first, will result in a deadlock. The static lock functions guarantee that two different strings will never point to the same lock, thus avoiding introducing unnecessary (and transparent!) synchronization between processes. Their disadvantage is the nature of their parameters (static strings), making them inappropriate in certain scenarios.

exported_functions.name: release_static_lock

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: key to be hashed in order to obtain the index of a static lock.

exported_functions.description: Release the static lock corresponding to "key". Nothing will happen if the lock is not acquired.

exported_mi_functions.name: rand_set_prop

parameters.name: prob_proc
parameters.description: the parameter should be a percent value (number from 0 to 99)

exported_mi_functions.description: Set the probability value to the given parameter.

exported_mi_functions.name: rand_reset_prob
exported_mi_functions.description: Reset the probability value to the inital start value.

exported_mi_functions.name: rand_get_prob
exported_mi_functions.description: Return the actual probability setting. The function return the actual probability value.

examples.code:
...
$ opensips-cli -x mi get\_prob
The actual probability is 50 percent.
...

exported_mi_functions.name: check_config_hash

return_value.description: The function returns 200 OK if the hash values are identical, 400 if there are not identical, 404 if no file for hashing has been configured and 500 on errors. Additional a short text message is printed.

exported_mi_functions.description: Check if the actual config file hash is identical to the stored one.

examples.code:
...
$ opensips-cli -x mi check\_config\_hash
The actual config file hash is identical to the stored one.
...

exported_mi_functions.name: get_config_hash

return_value.description: The function returns 200 OK and the hash value on success or 404 if no file for hashing has been configured.

exported_mi_functions.description: Return the stored config file hash.

exported_mi_functions.name: shv_set

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: type of the value (“int”: integer value; “str”: string value)

exported_mi_functions.description: Set the value of a shared variable ($shv(name)).

exported_mi_functions.name: shv_get

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: shared variable name. If this parameter is missing, all shared variables are returned.

exported_mi_functions.description: Get the value of a shared variable ($shv(name)).

examples.code:
...
$ opensips-cli -x mi shv\_get debug
$ opensips-cli -x mi shv\_get
...

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $env(name)
exported_pseudo_variables.description: This PV provides access to the environment variable 'name'.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $RANDOM
exported_pseudo_variables.description: Returns a random value from the [0 - 2^31) range.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $ctime(name)
exported_pseudo_variables.description: The PV provides access to broken-down time attributes.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $shv(name)
exported_pseudo_variables.description: It is a class of pseudo-variables stored in shared memory. The value of $shv(name) is visible across all opensips processes. Each “shv” has single value and it is initialized to integer 0. You can use “shvset” parameter to initialize the shared variable. The module exports a set of MI functions to get/set the value of shared variables.
